title: Research and innovation careers are expanding while STEM composition, renewal, mobility, and employment stability reveal uneven future capacity
source_unit: OECD, Research and Innovation Careers Observatory 2026: Key Indicators on Talent, Mobility and Working Conditions
geography: OECD countries and major research and innovation systems with comparative talent, mobility, labor-market, and working-condition indicators

denominator.unit: OECD employment and research-and-development workforce frame

rd_personnel_2024.unit: percent of employment represented by research and development personnel across OECD countries in 2024

rd_personnel_2015.unit: percent of employment represented by research and development personnel across OECD countries in 2015

career_direction.value: opportunities for highly skilled people to participate in research and innovation have grown considerably

renewal_risk.value: future supply is not guaranteed because several countries saw doctoral graduate numbers decline amid ageing and older qualified workforces

observations.method: OECD-EU Research and Innovation Careers Observatory comparative indicators on workforce size, composition, renewal, outcomes, and mobility.
observations.uncertainty: OECD aggregates conceal country, discipline, gender, sector, contract, and career-stage differences; workforce share does not measure innovation quality or worker experience directly.
observations.subgroup: Researchers, engineers, doctoral students, technicians, employers, universities, public laboratories, firms, and policymakers responsible for talent renewal.
observations.counterinterpretation: A growing R&I workforce can strengthen capacity if systems improve career quality, inclusion, research funding, and pathways between sectors.

denominator.unit: OECD master's, doctoral, STEM employment, and advanced-qualification frame

doctoral_degrees_2023.unit: more than doctoral degrees awarded across OECD countries in 2023

masters_degrees_2023.unit: more than master's degrees awarded across OECD countries in 2023

ict_employment_2024.unit: percent of OECD employment in ICT professional occupations in 2024

science_engineering_employment_2024.unit: percent of OECD employment in science and engineering professional occupations in 2024

doctoral_stem_share.value: the share of doctoral graduates in STEM fell from 48 percent in 2015 to 46 percent in 2023

observations.method: OECD education, employment, qualification, and occupation indicators assembled through the ReICO evidence base.
observations.uncertainty: Degree and occupation categories do not show field quality, skill use, migration selection, job tasks, or whether graduates enter research careers; comparisons vary by national classification.
observations.subgroup: STEM students, doctoral and master's graduates, ICT workers, science and engineering professionals, educators, firms, and research institutions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable or falling STEM shares in advanced degrees can reflect expansion of other valuable fields; policy should match skills to changing needs rather than maximize one category mechanically.

observations.period: 2026; doctorate labor outcomes and employment stability

denominator.unit: OECD doctorate-holder and master's-holder labor-market comparison frame

doctorate_employment.unit: percent-plus employment rate typically reported for doctorate holders in most countries

earnings_premium.unit: percent OECD-wide earnings premium of doctorate holders relative to master's degree holders

full_time.unit: percent of employed doctorate holders in full-time jobs on average across the OECD

stability_constraint.value: doctorate holders are slightly less likely than master's holders to hold indefinite contracts, reflecting fixed-term postdoctoral work in some systems

observations.method: OECD comparative labor-market indicators for doctorate and master's degree holders, including employment, earnings, hours, and contract status.
observations.uncertainty: Country differences, field, age, sector, selection into doctoral education, and contract definitions affect outcomes; aggregate premiums are not individual causal returns.
observations.subgroup: Doctorate holders, master's graduates, postdoctoral researchers, early-career scientists, universities, firms, and research funders.
observations.counterinterpretation: Strong average labor-market outcomes can coexist with early-career insecurity; longer-term career pathways and sector mobility may improve the value of advanced training.

denominator.unit: OECD internationally mobile graduates, researchers, and R&I evidence frame

mobile_masters.unit: percent of master's graduates who were internationally mobile across the OECD in 2023

mobile_doctorates.unit: percent of doctoral graduates who were internationally mobile across the OECD in 2023

prior_mobility_authors.unit: approximate percent of scientific authors affiliated with OECD countries in 2024 showing evidence of prior international mobility

evidence_priority.value: future evidence should track cross-sector and cross-border careers, critical-technology occupations, capabilities, motivations, working conditions, and long-term trajectories

observations.method: OECD mobility indicators and ReICO evidence agenda combining official statistics with proposed administrative, labor-market, and digital-trace sources.
observations.uncertainty: Mobility measures do not reveal who benefits, who is excluded, whether mobility is voluntary, or how mobility affects local research capacity; proposed digital traces are not equivalent to respondent data.
observations.subgroup: International students, mobile researchers, foreign-born doctorate holders, host institutions, sending countries, and workers considering research careers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Mobility can circulate knowledge and strengthen research linkages, while inclusive domestic career systems can retain talent and avoid treating migration as a zero-sum loss.

related_sources.claim: OECD science, technology, and innovation work provides complementary policy and indicator context.
Eurostat provides complementary European science, technology, and innovation statistics used in comparative evidence contexts.

boundary: This record adds a research-and-innovation labor route across talent supply, STEM composition, doctoral outcomes, contract stability, international mobility, and evidence gaps. It uses OECD comparative indicators and report synthesis, not respondent-level career histories, individual earnings panels, causal education returns, private workplace records, or proof that aggregate talent growth produces equitable innovation outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official OECD Research and Innovation Careers Observatory 2026 page reviewed for publication metadata, ReICO scope, R&D employment share, degrees, STEM composition, doctorate outcomes, contract stability, international mobility, and future evidence priorities.
